decisions.reason: F1 attributes a subcomodule of k[G] to the final line-stabilizer representation, although the supplier and Milne 4.27/4.28 pass from a subcomodule U to an exterior power of U. This strengthening is unlicensed and unnecessary: step 1.1 needs only the supplied finite-dimensional rational representation and its line. Removed the strengthening; the theorem and proof steps retain their full conclusions.

F1 wrongly extends finite presentation and standard smoothness to arbitrary localizations. For example k(x) cannot be finitely generated over k: finitely many rational generators lie in k[x,1/f], which omits inverses of irreducibles not dividing f. This false generalization is unused; GL2 and T invert the single elements det and ad. Added principal to restrict the assertion to the exact empty-equation presentation supplied, retaining all proof steps and quotient conclusions.

reviews.reason: The published line-stabilizer proof constructs an exterior-power rational representation and identifies H on every test algebra, including H=G. The dual-projective convention gives exactly that stabilizer. AC and smooth G satisfy the locally closed smooth-orbit lemma; its faithfully flat locally finitely presented map and kernel pair give the fppf quotient. The ambient closed diagonal pulls back to prove separatedness, and finite type and Yoneda uniqueness follow. Only F1 changed; Statement, dependencies, proof steps, contracts and page interface remain unchanged. This is a local review and repair, not independent review of the repair.

F1 now applies only to principal polynomial localizations, including exactly GL2 and its diagonal torus. The stabilizer calculation holds over every algebra. On the diagonal complement the universal line frames have unit wedge determinant, giving sections and actual U x T trivializations; this proves faithful flatness and local finite presentation. The natural kernel-pair inverse is g inverse g-prime, so the criterion represents the fppf quotient. The algebraically closed dimension calculation satisfies connectedness and smoothness hypotheses; the projection fibre over any y is P1 over kappa(y) minus its canonical rational point, and the K-point coset bijection follows for every extension. AC is retained. Only F1 changed; Example, dependencies, verification steps, contract and page remain unchanged. This is local review and repair, not independent review of the repair.
